subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Fourfold Pattern of Risk
description: A fast breakdown of The Fourfold Pattern of Risk for builders.

hook.text: Risk aversion or risk seeking? Prospect theory says it depends on two things: gain or loss, high or low probability.

buildup.text: High-probability gains: risk averse. Low-probability gains: risk seeking. Each combination flips behavior.

discovery.text: The fourfold pattern: four quadrants of probability and outcome domain create four distinct risk attitudes.

twist.text: This explains why people buy both lottery tickets and insurance. Different quadrants of the same framework.

climax.text: Identify which quadrant you're in before deciding. Your risk attitude isn't fixed; it shifts with context.

punchline.text: Four quadrants, four attitudes, one you.

quiz.question: What does the fourfold pattern predict?
options: Risk attitude depends on probability level and gain/loss domain
Only wealthy people can be risk-seeking

details.summary: The fourfold pattern describes four distinct risk attitudes depending on whether outcomes involve gains or losses and whether probabilities are high or low. It explains why people buy insurance against unlikely losses and lottery tickets for unlikely gains.
details.whyItMatters: The fourfold pattern resolves the paradox of people being both risk-averse and risk-seeking. It provides a unified framework explaining insurance purchases, lottery playing, litigation behavior, and corporate risk management.
takeaways: High probability gains produce risk aversion with preference for certainty
Low probability gains produce risk seeking seen in lottery purchases
Low probability losses produce risk aversion seen in insurance purchases

faq.question: Why do people buy both insurance and lottery tickets?
faq.answer: The fourfold pattern explains both: people overweight small probabilities. For losses, this overweighting makes unlikely disasters feel threatening enough to insure against. For gains, it makes unlikely jackpots feel possible enough to gamble on.

faq.question: What is the fourth quadrant of the fourfold pattern?
faq.answer: High probability losses produce risk-seeking behavior. When a large loss is almost certain, people prefer to gamble for a small chance of avoiding it entirely. This explains why defendants in strong cases against them reject fair settlements.
